items.name: TU Munich (TUM)
items.description: One of Germany's leading technical universities in engineering, computer science, and natural sciences.
history: TUM was founded in 1868 by King Ludwig II of Bavaria as the Polytechnische Schule München. Its name changed several times over the decades, becoming the Technische Hochschule München in 1901 and finally the Technische Universität München in 1970.

Today the university is a member of TU9, the alliance of Germany's nine leading technical universities, and holds "University of Excellence" status from the federal government. It maintains a comprehensive research infrastructure across engineering, computer science, natural sciences, and medicine.

TUM's campuses span three main areas: the historic main campus in central Munich, the Garching campus focused on natural sciences and engineering, and the Weihenstephan campus focused on agriculture and life sciences. The university has produced numerous Nobel laureates throughout its history.
highlights: Strong research infrastructure in engineering, computer science, and natural sciences
Member of the TU9 alliance and holder of "University of Excellence" status
Large, specialized research campuses in Garching and Weihenstephan
Home to some of Germany's most sought-after engineering programs
pros: A globally top-ranked name in engineering and technology
Close proximity and strong internship ties to major industry players like BMW and Siemens
Strong research infrastructure and funding opportunities
cons: Very high admission competition, especially in programs like computer science
Munich is one of Germany's most expensive cities
Crowded lecture halls in popular courses

items.name: LMU Munich
items.description: One of Germany's oldest and most established universities, strong in medicine, law, and social sciences.
history: LMU was founded in 1472 in Ingolstadt by Duke Ludwig IX of Bavaria. It moved to Landshut in 1800 and then to its current home in Munich in 1826 — the "Ludwig-Maximilians" in its name honors the two rulers associated with that journey.

One of Europe's oldest universities, LMU has been home to numerous Nobel laureates throughout its history, including Wilhelm Röntgen, Max Planck, and Werner Heisenberg. Members of the White Rose (Weiße Rose), the student resistance group that opposed the Nazi regime during World War II, were also LMU students.
Today, with a strong faculty in medicine, law, natural sciences, and social sciences, LMU teaches on a historic campus stretching along Ludwigstraße in the heart of Munich.
highlights: One of Germany's oldest and most prestigious universities
Strong research tradition in medicine, law, and natural sciences
Home to numerous Nobel laureates throughout its history
A city-center campus in the heart of Munich
pros: An extremely broad program range from the humanities to medicine
Strong international reputation for research
A vibrant student life in Munich
cons: High grade requirements (Numerus Clausus) and competition for popular subjects
Munich's high cost of living
Large student body can mean less individual attention in big introductory lectures

items.name: Humboldt University of Berlin
items.description: A research university with international recognition in the humanities and social sciences.
history: Founded in 1810 by the linguist and statesman Wilhelm von Humboldt, Humboldt University is Berlin's oldest university. Its founding gave rise to the "Humboldtian model," which champions the unity of teaching and research under the principle of academic freedom — a model that became the foundation of the modern research university worldwide.

Throughout its history, figures such as Albert Einstein, Max Planck, Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, and Karl Marx have been associated with the university, and numerous Nobel laureates have taught or studied there.

Located on Unter den Linden boulevard in the very center of Berlin, the university suffered heavy damage during World War II and stood within East Berlin during the country's division; its rebuilt historic main building remains the heart of the university today.
highlights: The institution where the modern research university concept was born
International recognition in the humanities and social sciences
Historical ties to figures like Einstein and Planck
A historic campus in central Berlin, on Unter den Linden
pros: A central Berlin location close to cultural and career opportunities
A strong academic reputation in the humanities and social sciences
A historic, internationally recognized name
cons: Berlin's fast-rising rents put pressure on student budgets
High admission competition for popular subjects
A large, bureaucratic university structure can feel impersonal at first

items.name: RWTH Aachen
items.description: One of Europe's leading technical universities in engineering and computer science.
history: Founded in 1870 as the Polytechnicum, RWTH Aachen is today a member of the TU9 alliance and one of Germany's largest technical universities. Its location near the Belgian and Dutch borders has given the university a strong, international network of industry partnerships.

Known for its close ties to industry in automotive and mechanical engineering, RWTH Aachen also takes an innovative approach to student services: its iconic SuperC building, opened in 2009, serves as a central hub for student affairs and advising.

With a high share of international students and a wide range of English-taught master's programs, the university is one of the most popular destinations in Germany for international students seeking an engineering education.
highlights: Strong industry ties in automotive and mechanical engineering
Member of the TU9 alliance of technical universities
An innovative approach to student services via the iconic SuperC building
High share of international students, with English-taught master's programs
pros: Strong industry-university ties in engineering and a high post-graduation employment rate
A lower cost of living compared to Munich or Berlin
A large, active international student community
cons: Aachen is a smaller city compared to Berlin or Munich
Engineering programs are demanding and intensive
Limited spots and high competition in some master's programs

items.name: University of Mannheim
items.description: Home to one of Germany's top business and economics programs.
history: Founded in 1907 as the Handelshochschule Mannheim (Mannheim Commercial College), the institution was established through the efforts of then-mayor Otto Beck and economist Eberhard Gothein. Absorbed into the University of Heidelberg under the National Socialist regime in 1933, it reopened after the war in 1946 and gained full university status in 1967.

The university is housed in the historic Mannheim Palace (Schloss Mannheim), Europe's second-largest Baroque palace after Versailles — a distinctive setting that visually sets it apart from other German business schools.
Today, Mannheim consistently ranks among the top German universities for business and economics, with a strong international exchange network and a research-driven academic culture.
highlights: One of Germany's top business and economics faculties
Housed in the historic Mannheim Palace, Europe's second-largest Baroque palace
A strong international exchange program network
A research-driven academic culture with international recognition
pros: One of Germany's top-ranked business and economics faculties
Proximity to major companies like SAP and BASF, with strong corporate ties
A unique learning environment in a historic palace campus
cons: Academic focus is largely limited to business, economics, and social sciences, with few STEM options
Mannheim is a quieter city compared to Berlin or Munich
An intense, competitive grading culture in the business faculty

items.name: Munich University of Applied Sciences
items.description: A Fachhochschule with strong industry ties in applied engineering and business programs.
history: Formed in 1971 through the merger of seven technical and vocational colleges, Hochschule München is today Bavaria's second-largest university of applied sciences (Fachhochschule).

Offering an education tightly linked to industry in engineering, design, and business, the university introduces students to the working world before graduation through applied project work and mandatory internship periods.
The campus's landmark "Roter Würfel" (Red Cube) building houses the design faculty and is part of a community of around 18,000 students.
highlights: Bavaria's second-largest university of applied sciences (Fachhochschule)
Strong industry ties in engineering, design, and business
An applied, internship-driven education model
A community of around 18,000 students
pros: A practice-oriented curriculum backed by mandatory internships
Strong regional industry connections in Bavaria
A more direct, career-focused path than a theory-heavy Universität
cons: A Fachhochschule degree can carry somewhat less prestige than a Universität degree for academic/research careers
Limited option to pursue a doctorate directly
Munich's high cost of living

items.name: Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences
items.description: Applied programs in business and information technology in the financial hub of Frankfurt.
history: Founded on August 1, 1971, Frankfurt UAS is today one of Germany's largest universities of applied sciences, home to more than 15,000 students.

Located in Germany's financial capital, the university leverages its position to build close partnerships with the banking, finance, and IT sectors, offering industry-facing programs in business, information technology, engineering, and social work.
Through applied research projects and mandatory industry internships, the university aims to give its students a strong, direct path into the job market after graduation.
highlights: Centrally located in Frankfurt, Germany's financial capital
Applied programs in business, IT, and engineering
Close partnerships with the banking and finance sector
A campus community of more than 15,000 students
pros: Direct access to Germany's banking and finance job market
An applied curriculum backed by a strong internship culture
A relatively diverse student body
cons: A less internationally famous name than research universities
No direct route to a doctorate
Frankfurt has a high cost of living relative to smaller German cities

items.name: DHBW (Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University)
items.city: Stuttgart, Mannheim, Karlsruhe, and other campuses
items.description: The pioneer of the dual studium model in Germany, alternating theory and practice in three-month cycles.
history: DHBW's roots trace back to the Berufsakademie Baden-Württemberg, founded in 1974. Conceived as an entirely new type of educational institution at the time, it grew quickly to include locations across the state.

In 2009, the Baden-Württemberg state parliament granted this 35-year-old, successful model full higher-education status, transforming the Berufsakademie into the Duale Hochschule Baden-Württemberg (DHBW). By that point, enrollment had surpassed 23,000 students, working with more than 8,000 partner companies.

Today, spread across numerous campuses throughout Baden-Württemberg and working with thousands of partner companies, DHBW offers students a model that alternates theory and practice in three-month cycles, and is considered the pioneer of Germany's dual studium system.
highlights: The pioneering institution behind Germany's dual studium model
A network of thousands of partner companies
Numerous campus locations across Baden-Württemberg
A state-recognized evolution of a model with more than 35 years of history
pros: Earning a regular salary from a partner company while studying removes tuition pressure
Guaranteed practical work experience, often leading to a job offer at graduation
Theory and practice are tightly integrated
cons: You need to secure a partner-company contract before applying, an extra step in the process
The program is highly structured, leaving little flexibility for electives or exchange semesters
An intensive pace with almost no long breaks between theory and practice blocks

items.name: IU International University of Applied Sciences
items.description: One of Germany's largest private higher education institutions for dual studium and distance learning.
history: Founded in 1998 in Bad Honnef and Bonn as the Internationale Fachhochschule with just 23 students in its first year, the institution entered a period of rapid growth. It merged with the Adam-Ries-Fachhochschule in 2013, was renamed IUBH Internationale Hochschule in 2017, and took its current name, IU International University of Applied Sciences, in 2021.
Through this rapid expansion, IU has become Germany's largest university by student enrollment, surpassing 130,000 students as of 2025.

IU is known for its dual studium and distance-learning programs, offering in-person study at more than 24 campuses across Germany while also serving students who need flexible schedules through a strong digital learning infrastructure.
highlights: Germany's largest university by student enrollment
24+ campuses plus strong distance-learning options
A wide partner-company network for dual studium
Rapid, continuous growth since its founding in 1998
pros: Flexible study formats across dual studium, distance learning, and on-campus study
A wide network of locations across Germany
A modern digital learning infrastructure
cons: As a young, fast-growing private institution, it carries less traditional academic prestige than public universities
Tuition fees apply, unlike most public universities
Rapid growth has drawn some scrutiny over teaching quality consistency

items.name: FOM University of Applied Sciences
items.description: One of Germany's largest private higher education institutions for students who work while studying.
history: Founded in 1993 and receiving official state recognition on September 18, 1993, FOM opened its doors in 1994. Its founding purpose was to let full-time working students pursue a university education through evening and weekend programs.

Thanks to this focus, FOM grew rapidly and today operates study centers in more than 30 cities across Germany, making it one of the country's largest private higher education institutions with over 47,000 students.

With a broad range of business and economics programs, FOM also offers flexible study options that include the dual studium model, serving students who want to combine working life with a university education.
highlights: Evening and weekend programs for working students
Study centers in more than 30 German cities
One of Germany's largest private higher education institutions, with 47,000+ students
A broad range of business and economics programs
pros: Purpose-built for students who want to keep working full-time
A large network of local study centers close to home
Strong ties to regional employers
cons: Tuition fees apply
The evening/weekend schedule can be demanding alongside a full-time job
Less of a traditional campus/student-life experience than a full-time university

items.name: Heidelberg University (Ruprecht-Karls-Universität)
items.description: Founded in 1386, Germany's oldest and one of its most prestigious research universities.
history: Heidelberg University was founded on October 18, 1386, when Elector Ruprecht I received the Pope's permission to establish it. It is Germany's oldest university and the third to be founded in the Holy Roman Empire. Modeled after the University of Paris, it initially comprised four faculties — philosophy, theology, law, and medicine — with the Dutch scholar Marsilius of Inghen, who came from Paris, serving as its first rector.

Also known as "Ruperto Carola," the university has been home to leading scientists throughout its history, including Robert Bunsen, Hermann von Helmholtz, Gustav Kirchhoff, and Max Weber; to date, its professors have been awarded 11 Nobel Prizes.

Set in the historic city center in the shadow of Heidelberg Castle, the university is today regarded as one of Europe's strongest research universities, offering bachelor's, master's, and doctoral programs across 12 faculties and around 100 disciplines.
highlights: Germany's oldest and one of Europe's most established universities
11 Nobel Prizes awarded to its professors to date
A broad academic range across 12 faculties and around 100 disciplines
A campus in the historic city center, in the shadow of Heidelberg Castle
pros: Germany's oldest and one of Europe's most prestigious research universities
An exceptionally strong faculty in medicine and the natural sciences
A beautiful, historic town with a strong student culture
cons: Very high admission competition for medicine and top programs
Heidelberg is a small city with a limited job market outside academia and pharma
High demand pushes up student housing prices despite the city's small size

items.name: University of Tübingen
items.description: Founded in 1477, a classic German university-town institution strong in medicine and the natural sciences.
history: The University of Tübingen was founded in 1477 by Count Eberhard VI, following a 1476 bull from Pope Sixtus IV. It initially comprised four faculties — theology, law, medicine, and philosophy — and fourteen professorships in total. Philipp Melanchthon, one of the leading figures of the Reformation, played an important role in shaping the university's academic direction.

Over the centuries, Tübingen has counted astronomer Johannes Kepler, poet Friedrich Hölderlin, and philosophers Friedrich Schelling and G.W.F. Hegel among its students. Pope Benedict XVI also briefly studied theology there in his youth.

Located in the heart of a historic town on the Neckar River, the university today carries a strong academic tradition in medicine, natural sciences, and the humanities, having produced numerous Nobel laureates, particularly in medicine and chemistry.
highlights: An unbroken academic tradition dating back to 1477
Alma mater of historic figures like Kepler, Hölderlin, and Hegel
A strong Nobel Prize track record in medicine and chemistry
A classic German university-town campus on the Neckar River
pros: A strong reputation in medicine and the natural sciences
A classic, tight-knit university town where student life is central
High research output relative to its size
cons: The small-town setting means fewer big-city career and internship opportunities nearby
Competitive admission for programs like medicine and psychology
Limited English-taught bachelor's options; most programs are German-taught

items.name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)
items.description: A research-driven technology university carrying the legacy of Germany's first technical higher-education institution.
history: KIT's roots trace back to the Fridericiana, founded in 1825 as Germany's first "Technische Hochschule" — the Universität Karlsruhe. It was here that Heinrich Hertz first experimentally demonstrated electromagnetic waves, and automobile pioneer Carl Benz studied at this historic institution.

In 2009, an act passed by the Baden-Württemberg state parliament merged the Universität Karlsruhe with Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe, a large-scale research institution founded in 1956, forming today's Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT).

Through this merger, KIT carries out both the teaching and research duties of a state university and the mission of a large-scale research institution within the Helmholtz Association, making it one of Germany's most comprehensive centers for technology and engineering research.
highlights: Carries the legacy of Germany's first technical higher-education institution, founded in 1825
Formed in 2009 through the merger of a university and a large-scale research institution
Also carries out large-scale research duties within the Helmholtz Association
Historical ties to figures like Heinrich Hertz and Carl Benz
pros: Combines university teaching with large-scale Helmholtz research facilities
A strong reputation in engineering, computer science, and energy research
Karlsruhe has a lower cost of living than Munich or Stuttgart
cons: Karlsruhe has less international name recognition abroad than Munich or Berlin
The engineering course load is demanding
The dual university/research-center structure can feel bureaucratically complex

items.name: University of Freiburg
items.description: Founded in 1457, a Habsburg-legacy university strong in philosophy and the social sciences.
history: The University of Freiburg was established by a charter issued by Albert VI of the House of Habsburg on September 21, 1457, making it the second university founded in Habsburg territory after the University of Vienna. From its founding, the university taught theology, law, and medicine, along with the "Artes Liberales" (liberal arts), which formed the basis of today's faculty of humanities.

Originally named the "Albertina," the university's continued existence was secured in 1818 by a significant gift from Grand Duke Ludwig of Baden, on which occasion it was renamed the Albert-Ludwigs-Universität, its name today. As Germany's fifth-oldest university, Freiburg built a strong tradition in philosophy, philology, historical research, economics, and law.

Associated with figures such as Martin Heidegger, Edmund Husserl, Max Weber, Walter Eucken, and Nobel laureate Friedrich Hayek, Freiburg continues to carry this deep-rooted academic identity in those disciplines today.
highlights: Germany's fifth-oldest university
An unbroken tradition since 1457, rooted in Habsburg heritage
A strong history in philosophy through figures like Heidegger and Husserl
A strong economics tradition that includes Nobel laureate Friedrich Hayek
pros: A strong reputation in philosophy, law, and environmental/natural sciences
Freiburg is consistently rated among Germany's most livable, sunniest cities
Proximity to the Black Forest and the French/Swiss border offers exchange opportunities
cons: A smaller job market than Berlin or Munich for graduates who want to stay locally
Competitive admission for popular humanities and law programs
Fewer large-scale industry partnerships than technical universities

items.name: University of Göttingen
items.description: Associated with 45 Nobel laureates, a research university at the heart of the "city of science," Göttingen.
history: Founded in 1734 by George II, King of Great Britain and Elector of Hanover, the university began lectures that same year, with its official inauguration following in 1737. Established in keeping with Enlightenment ideals, it became one of the pioneering institutions to free scientific research from church censorship.

In the 19th century, the university counted mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss and the Brothers Grimm among its faculty. In 1837, seven professors — including the Brothers Grimm — were removed from their posts after protesting the King of Hanover's expansion of his powers; the episode became known in history as the "Göttingen Seven" (Göttinger Sieben).

Göttingen is associated with 45 Nobel laureates, from quantum mechanics pioneer Max Born to mathematician Emmy Noether, 14 of whom were honored for work carried out at Göttingen itself. The oldest university in the state of Lower Saxony, Göttingen today sits at the heart of a city that carries the nickname "City of Science," with around 26,000 students.
highlights: A strong scientific tradition associated with 45 Nobel laureates
A mathematical legacy spanning Carl Friedrich Gauss to Emmy Noether
The oldest university in the state of Lower Saxony
A campus of around 26,000 students at the heart of the "City of Science"
pros: An outstanding Nobel Prize legacy and a strong reputation in natural sciences and mathematics
A close-knit "city of science" atmosphere built around the university
A relatively affordable cost of living for a university town
cons: Göttingen is a small city with limited big-city amenities and job market
Some programs are strongly German-taught and require solid German proficiency
Fewer international corporate employers nearby compared to major cities

items.name: University of Bonn
items.description: Founded in 1818, a well-established Rhineland university housed in a former electoral palace.
history: Founded on October 18, 1818, by King Frederick William III of Prussia as the Rhine University, the University of Bonn is the direct successor to the Academy of the Prince-Elector of Cologne, founded in 1777. Inspired by Wilhelm von Humboldt's principles of academic freedom and the unity of research and teaching, it quickly became one of Germany's most respected institutions.

In the 1930s, the Nazi regime forced many Jewish scholars and dissidents to leave the university; the 1944 bombing of Bonn then destroyed much of the campus. In the postwar period, the university was rebuilt and restored to its former standing.

The university's main building sits in the former Kurfürstliches Schloss (Electoral Palace), overlooking the Hofgarten park. Associated with figures such as physicist Heinrich Hertz, chemist August Kekulé, and former German Chancellor Konrad Adenauer, Bonn is today one of Germany's leading universities, with around 36,000 students.
highlights: A historic main building in a former electoral palace, overlooking the Hofgarten park
A founding philosophy inspired by Humboldt's principles of academic freedom
Historical ties to figures like Heinrich Hertz and Konrad Adenauer
One of Germany's leading universities, with around 36,000 students
pros: A strong program in law, economics, mathematics, and natural sciences
Benefits from the presence of UN institutions and international organizations in the city
A historic palace campus with a strong academic tradition
cons: Bonn's job market is smaller than Berlin's, despite the international organizations present
Competitive admission for law and medicine
A large student body can mean crowded introductory lectures

items.name: University of Cologne
items.description: Founded in 1388, one of Germany's largest traditional universities by enrollment.
history: Founded in 1388, the University of Cologne was the fourth university established in the Holy Roman Empire, after Prague (1348), Vienna (1365), and Heidelberg (1386). Its founding charter was signed by Pope Urban VI, and teaching began on January 6, 1389.

Closed during the French occupation in 1798, the university was re-established in 1919 as the "Neue Universität" (New University) — a refounding that laid the groundwork for its modern identity today.

With more than 44,000 students today, Cologne is Germany's largest traditional university by enrollment. Across six faculties and 137 degree programs, it maintains a strong academic tradition, particularly in law, economics, and the social sciences.
highlights: The fourth university founded in the Holy Roman Empire (1388)
Re-established as the "Neue Universität" in 1919
Germany's largest traditional university by enrollment, with 44,000+ students
A strong academic tradition in law, economics, and social sciences (WiSo)
pros: A very broad program offering across six faculties
A strong reputation in law, economics, and social sciences (WiSo)
Cologne is a large, lively city with a strong job market and cultural scene
cons: A very large student body can mean less individual attention and crowded lecture halls
Administrative processes can feel bureaucratic given the university's size
Competitive admission for popular subjects like medicine, law, and psychology

items.name: Technical University of Berlin
items.description: A technical university whose roots reach back to 1770, formally re-founded in 1946 to mark its present identity.
history: TU Berlin's roots trace back to the Königliche Bergakademie (Royal Mining Academy), founded in 1770, the Königliche Bauakademie (Royal Building Academy), founded in 1799, and the Königliche Gewerbeakademie (Royal Trade Academy), founded in 1821. These three institutions merged in 1879 to form the Königlich Technische Hochschule zu Berlin, with the Mining Academy incorporated in 1916.

In 1946, in a deliberate effort to document a clear break from its National Socialist past, the institution was positioned not as a reopening but as a conscious new founding, taking the name Technische Universität Berlin from that point on — the date now recognized as the university's official founding.

A member of the TU9 alliance, the university is associated with figures such as computer pioneer Konrad Zuse and chemists Carl Bosch and Fritz Haber. Located in Berlin's Charlottenburg district, TU Berlin today maintains a strong research culture in engineering and the natural sciences.
highlights: A long history reaching back to 1770 and the Royal Mining Academy
A deliberate 1946 re-founding to mark a break from its Nazi-era past
Member of the TU9 alliance of technical universities
Historical ties to figures like Konrad Zuse and Fritz Haber
pros: Combines a top technical education with all of Berlin's career and cultural opportunities
Strong ties to Berlin's growing tech and startup scene
A TU9 member with a strong engineering and computer science reputation
cons: Berlin's sharply rising rents make student housing competitive to find
Large classes in popular engineering and computer science programs
Administrative processes can be slow given the university's size

items.name: University of Oxford
items.description: The oldest university in the English-speaking world; a globally recognized name in nearly every field.
history: Teaching is known to have existed at Oxford as early as 1096, making it the oldest university in the English-speaking world. Oxford grew rapidly after 1167, when King Henry II of England banned English students from attending the University of Paris.

The university has a unique structure made up of more than 39 independent colleges, the oldest of which were founded between 1249 and 1264. Oxford's alumni include numerous Nobel laureates, world leaders, and authors.
highlights: The oldest university in the English-speaking world
A unique structure of 39+ independent colleges
Global recognition in nearly every academic field
pros: One of the world's most prestigious academic brands, opening global career doors after graduation
Intensive academic support through small-group tutorials via the college system
In-depth research opportunities across nearly every discipline
cons: Admission is extremely competitive, with a separate interview stage
Oxford is a small city with more limited amenities than the UK's larger cities
The academic workload and pace are intense, with short terms requiring heavy study loads

items.name: University of Cambridge
items.description: The world's fourth-oldest university, with an outstanding Nobel Prize legacy in science and mathematics.
history: Founded in 1209 when scholars fleeing a dispute in Oxford settled in the town of Cambridge, the university received a royal charter from King Henry III in 1231. It is today recognized as the fourth-oldest university in the world in continuous operation.

Made up of 31 independent colleges, Cambridge has been home to some of the most important names in the history of science, from Isaac Newton to Charles Darwin, Stephen Hawking to Alan Turing; more than 120 Nobel Prizes are associated with the university.
highlights: The world's fourth-oldest university in continuous operation
Shaped the history of science through figures like Newton, Darwin, and Hawking
31 colleges and 120+ Nobel Prizes associated with the university
pros: World-leading academic reputation in the sciences, mathematics, and engineering
Intensive academic support through small-group supervisions via the college system
Strong research funding and world-class laboratory facilities
cons: Admission is extremely competitive, requiring an interview and additional exams for some subjects
Cambridge is a quiet, small university town compared to larger cities
Short, intensive terms require a demanding pace of study

items.name: Imperial College London
items.description: A London-based, globally ranked STEM university focused on science, engineering, medicine, and business.
history: Imperial College was founded in 1907 through the merger of the Royal College of Science, the Royal School of Mines, and the City and Guilds College, with roots reaching back to the Royal College of Chemistry founded in 1845. It operated as part of the University of London for most of its history, becoming fully independent in 2007.
Alongside its main campus in South Kensington, Imperial spans nine campuses across London and is recognized as a world-leading institution in science, engineering, medicine, and business (STEMB).
highlights: A world-leading institution in science, engineering, medicine, and business (STEMB)
Nine campuses across London
Gained independence from the University of London in 2007
pros: World-leading academic reputation in engineering, medicine, and the natural sciences
Direct proximity to London's finance and tech sectors, with strong internship ties
An intensely research-focused academic culture closely tied to industry
cons: Admission is highly competitive, especially in engineering and medicine
London is one of the UK's most expensive cities
The program offering is heavily STEM-focused, with limited humanities options

items.name: University College London (UCL)
items.description: London's first university, founded without regard to religion or social status.
history: Founded on 11 February 1826 as "London University," UCL was designed as a secular alternative to Oxford and Cambridge at the time. It became England's first university to admit students regardless of their religious beliefs.

As London's first university, UCL also took a pioneering role by including practical sciences in its curriculum and offering women higher education on equal terms with men. Today it has a strong faculty in law, medicine, architecture, and engineering.
highlights: England's first university to admit students regardless of religion
London's first university
A strong faculty in law, medicine, architecture, and engineering
pros: A central London campus with direct access to cultural and career opportunities
A very broad program range with strong interdisciplinary options
A strong, diverse international student community
cons: London's high cost of living can strain a student budget
A large student body can mean crowded classes in some courses
Competitive admission for popular subjects

items.name: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE)
items.description: One of the world's most influential names in social sciences, economics, and political science.
history: Founded in 1895 by Sidney and Beatrice Webb as a night school for the working class, LSE quickly grew into one of the world's leading institutions in the social sciences. It became a college of the University of London in 1900.

Open to women and men on equal terms from its founding and welcoming students from abroad, LSE has been associated with 21 Nobel Prizes (in Peace, Economics, and Literature) and is recognized as an institution that has produced world leaders.
highlights: A world-renowned name in social sciences, economics, and political science
An education built on gender equality since its founding
An academic legacy associated with 21 Nobel Prizes
pros: World-leading reputation in economics, political science, and international relations
Direct proximity to London's finance and policy circles
A highly international, multicultural student community
cons: The program offering is largely limited to social sciences, with no STEM options
London's high cost of living
An intense, academically demanding environment

items.name: King's College London
items.description: Founded by King George IV and the Duke of Wellington, a London university strong in medicine and law.
history: Founded in 1829 under the leadership of King George IV and the Duke of Wellington, victor of the Battle of Waterloo, King's College London became one of the two founding colleges of the University of London in 1836.

Having merged over time with Chelsea College, Queen Elizabeth College, and the medical schools of Guy's and St Thomas' Hospitals, King's today has a strong faculty particularly in medicine, dentistry, law, and international relations.
highlights: A well-established London university founded by King George IV and the Duke of Wellington
One of the two founding colleges of the University of London
A strong faculty in medicine, dentistry, and law
pros: A strong academic reputation in medicine, law, and international relations
Multiple campuses in central London along the River Thames
Medical education backed by strong hospital and clinical partnerships
cons: London's high cost of living
Competitive admission for subjects like medicine and law
Campuses are spread across the city rather than a single central site

items.name: University of Edinburgh
items.description: A center of the Scottish Enlightenment and the oldest civic-founded university in the English-speaking world.
history: Founded by a charter from King James VI in 1582 at the initiative of the Edinburgh Town Council, the university opened its doors in 1583 as "The Town's College." It is the oldest university in the English-speaking world founded by a city council rather than a church or monarch.

A hub of the 18th-century Scottish Enlightenment, Edinburgh counted thinkers like David Hume among its ranks; today it carries a strong academic reputation in medicine, veterinary medicine, artificial intelligence, and literature.

A center of the Scottish Enlightenment
A strong academic reputation in medicine, veterinary medicine, and AI
pros: A strong academic reputation in medicine, veterinary medicine, and computer science/AI
A high quality of life in Edinburgh, a historic and lively capital city
Strong research infrastructure and a large international student community
cons: Scotland's weather is variable and generally cool year-round
Competitive admission for popular subjects
Edinburgh has a more limited corporate job market than London

items.name: University of Manchester
items.description: A university with an industrial legacy, known for splitting the atom and discovering graphene.
history: With roots tracing back to the Manchester Mechanics' Institute, founded in 1824, the university took its current form in 2004 through the merger of the Victoria University of Manchester and UMIST (the University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology).

The university where the structure of the atom was discovered and where graphene was first isolated in 2010, Manchester has strong industry ties in engineering, materials science, and business; more than 25 Nobel laureates are associated with the university.
highlights: The university where graphene was first isolated
A strong scientific legacy associated with 25+ Nobel laureates
A modern university formed by the 2004 merger of two established institutions
pros: Strong research infrastructure in engineering, materials science, and natural sciences
A more affordable cost of living compared to London
A vibrant student life in Manchester, a large and lively city
cons: A very large student body can mean crowded classes in some courses
Northern England's climate is more variable and rainy than London's
Competitive admission for popular engineering and medicine programs

items.name: University of Bristol
items.description: The first higher education institution in England to admit men and women on equal terms.
history: Founded in 1876 as University College, Bristol, the institution became the first higher education institution in England to admit men and women on equal terms. It gained full university status with a royal charter in 1909.
Home to figures like physicist Paul Dirac, Bristol today has a strong research faculty in engineering, natural sciences, and robotics, with close ties to the city's creative and tech-driven economy.

A strong scientific legacy including physicist Paul Dirac
A strong research faculty in engineering, robotics, and natural sciences

items.name: University of Amsterdam (UvA)
items.description: One of the Netherlands' largest research universities, in the heart of Amsterdam.
history: Founded in 1632 when Gerardus Vossius opened the Athenaeum Illustre, UvA is the fourth-oldest academic institution still in operation in the Netherlands. It gained full university status in the 19th century.

Teaching in the very center of Amsterdam and at the Science Park campus, UvA has a strong research faculty in social sciences, law, humanities, and natural sciences, and is regarded as one of the Netherlands' largest universities.

Campuses in central Amsterdam and at Science Park
A strong academic reputation in social sciences and law

items.name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU)
items.description: Amsterdam's second major university, founded on the principle of independence from the state and church.
history: Founded in 1880 under the leadership of theologian and statesman Abraham Kuyper as a university independent ("vrije," or "free") from the state and church, VU was launched at a founding assembly held in Amsterdam's Nieuwe Kerk.
Today VU teaches on a modern campus near Amsterdam's Zuidas business district and has a strong faculty in medicine, business, and natural sciences.

A modern campus near Amsterdam's Zuidas business district
A strong faculty in medicine, business, and natural sciences

items.name: TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
items.description: The Netherlands' oldest and largest technical university.
history: Founded in 1842 by King William II as a royal academy originally meant to train civil servants for the Dutch East Indies, TU Delft became a full technical university in 1905.

Today one of Europe's leading technical universities in engineering, architecture, and computer science, TU Delft is also known for its expertise in water management and marine engineering — a field directly tied to the Netherlands' long fight against the sea.

Consistently top-ranked across Europe in engineering and architecture
Specialized expertise in water management and marine engineering

items.name: Utrecht University
items.description: One of the Netherlands' largest research universities, with a broad program range.
history: Founded in 1636, Utrecht University attracted large numbers of foreign students in the 17th and 18th centuries, particularly from England and Scotland.

Today teaching at the De Uithof (Utrecht Science Park) campus, the university is recognized as one of the Netherlands' most comprehensive research universities in medicine, law, natural sciences, and social sciences.

A modern campus at De Uithof (Utrecht Science Park)
A comprehensive research university in medicine, law, and natural sciences

items.name: Leiden University
items.description: The Netherlands' oldest university, founded in 1575 by William of Orange.
history: Founded in 1575 by William of Orange during the struggle for independence from Spain, Leiden University is the oldest university in the Netherlands.

Building a strong academic tradition in law, international relations, and archaeology, Leiden's campus stretches along the historic Rapenburg canal and sits close to the Dutch government and international institutions in The Hague.

A strong tradition in law, international relations, and archaeology

items.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
items.description: A Rotterdam-based university with one of Europe's top schools of business and economics.
history: Founded in 1913 as the Nederlandsche Handels-Hoogeschool (Netherlands School of Commerce), the university took its current name in 1973, honoring the humanist thinker Erasmus.

Home to the Rotterdam School of Management (RSM), regarded as one of Europe's top business and economics schools, the university is also a strong name in health sciences through its medical faculty, Erasmus MC.

A strong medical faculty through Erasmus MC
Named after the humanist thinker Erasmus

items.name: Maastricht University
items.description: A highly international university known for its Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model.
history: Founded on January 9, 1976, Maastricht University is one of the Netherlands' youngest universities. From its founding, it adopted the innovative Problem-Based Learning model, in which students learn in small groups through real-world problems.

Thanks to its location near the Belgian and German borders, Maastricht has an exceptionally international student profile and carries a strong academic reputation in European studies, business, and medicine.

One of the Netherlands' most international student populations
A strong academic reputation in European studies, business, and medicine

items.name: Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e)
items.description: A technical university founded to supply Philips with engineers, at the heart of the Netherlands' "Silicon Valley."
history: Founded in 1956 by the Dutch government as the Technische Hogeschool Eindhoven, with the goal of training the qualified engineers needed by electronics giant Philips' research laboratories, the university opened its doors in 1957.
Today at the heart of Eindhoven's "Brainport" tech region, TU/e offers an industry-integrated education in electrical engineering, computer science, and design.

A campus at the heart of Eindhoven's "Brainport" tech region

items.name: Sorbonne Université
items.description: Paris's most recognized academic brand, with roots reaching back to 1257.
history: Born in 1257 as a college founded by Robert de Sorbon for poor students, the Sorbonne grew over time into one of Europe's leading centers of science and culture. Closed during the French Revolution, it was re-established by Napoleon in 1806.

Today's Sorbonne Université was formed in 2018 through the merger of Paris-Sorbonne University (Paris IV) and Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University (Paris VI), bringing together the humanities, medicine, and natural sciences under one comprehensive structure.

items.name: Université PSL (Paris Sciences & Lettres)
items.description: A select alliance of Paris institutions bringing together storied names like the Collège de France.
history: Founded in 2010, Université PSL brings together numerous established, elite institutions under one roof, with roots reaching back to the Collège de France, founded in 1530; it formally became a full university in 2019.
Home to 11 founding institutions including the École Normale Supérieure, Paris Dauphine, and the Institut Curie, PSL consistently ranks as France's top university in international rankings.

items.name: Sciences Po Paris
items.description: France's most influential school of political science and international relations, alma mater to numerous heads of state.
history: Founded in 1872 in the aftermath of France's defeat by Prussia, with the goal of training a new political and administrative elite, Sciences Po quickly became one of the central institutions of French public life.

Alma mater to numerous French presidents including Emmanuel Macron and Jacques Chirac, Sciences Po is today a globally recognized name in political science, international relations, and public policy.

items.name: École Polytechnique
items.description: Founded during the French Revolution, France's most elite "Grande École" for engineering.
history: Founded in 1794 by mathematician Gaspard Monge in response to the French Revolution's need for engineers and high-level officials, École Polytechnique became a military academy under Napoleon in 1804.

Also known by its nickname "X," the school admits students from across France through an extremely selective entrance exam; today, at its campus in Palaiseau near Paris, it carries a world-class reputation in engineering, mathematics, and physics.

items.name: HEC Paris
items.description: Founded by the Paris Chamber of Commerce, one of Europe's top business schools.
history: Founded in 1881 by the Paris Chamber of Commerce and Industry, HEC Paris set out to become one of France's most established "Grandes Écoles" for business and commerce.
Today teaching at its château campus in Jouy-en-Josas near Paris, HEC Paris is consistently ranked among Europe's top business schools for its MBA and master's programs.

items.name: Université Paris-Saclay
items.description: A young but powerful university bringing together one of France's largest research clusters.
history: Home to numerous institutions with roots reaching back to 1150 and the founding of the University of Paris, Paris-Saclay was formally founded in 2014 and took its current structure in 2020.

Bringing together institutions like the École Normale Supérieure Paris-Saclay and the CEA research center, the university consistently ranks among the world's best in international rankings for mathematics, physics, and computer science.

items.name: Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1
items.description: One of France's largest science and medicine universities outside Paris.
history: With roots reaching back to a Faculty of Sciences founded in 1808, the University of Lyon was formally established in 1896 through the merger of several faculties. It split into three independent universities in 1970, one of which became Lyon 1, named after physiologist Claude Bernard.
Today one of France's strongest universities outside Paris in medicine, natural sciences, and sports science, Lyon 1 teaches in France's second-largest city, Lyon.

items.name: Aix-Marseille Université
items.description: Founded in 1409, reunified in 2012 to become the largest university in the French-speaking world.
history: Founded in 1409 at the initiative of Louis II of Anjou, Count of Provence, the university was closed during the French Revolution and later re-established as separate institutions in Aix and Marseille.

Reunified in 2012, Aix-Marseille Université became the largest university in the French-speaking world with around 70,000 students, carrying a strong academic reputation in law, medicine, and Mediterranean studies.

items.name: ETH Zurich
items.description: Continental Europe's top technical university, alma mater to Albert Einstein.
history: Founded in 1854 as a federal polytechnic school and opening its doors in 1855, ETH Zurich was inspired by the model of the École polytechnique in Paris.

Counting Albert Einstein among its alumni, ETH Zurich is associated with more than 20 Nobel laureates and is today regarded as continental Europe's top technical university in engineering, natural sciences, and computer science.

items.name: EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne)
items.description: A French-speaking regional technical university on Lake Geneva, known for its iconic architecture.
history: Founded in 1853 as the École Spéciale de Lausanne, the school took its current name, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, in 1969, becoming one of Switzerland's two federal institutes of technology alongside ETH Zurich.
Known for its campus on Lake Geneva and its iconic Rolex Learning Center building, EPFL carries a world-class research reputation in computer science, materials engineering, and life sciences.

items.name: University of Zurich (UZH)
items.description: Europe's first university founded independently of a church or sovereign.
history: Formed in 1833 from the merger of colleges of theology, law, and medicine with roots reaching back to 1525, the University of Zurich was the first university in Europe founded independently of a church or a sovereign.
Switzerland's largest university, UZH has a strong faculty in medicine, law, and economics, and is associated with numerous Nobel laureates.

items.name: University of Geneva (UNIGE)
items.description: Founded by John Calvin, the university of Geneva, the city of international institutions.
history: Founded in 1559 by reformist theologian John Calvin as a school of theology, the University of Geneva shed its religious ties and gained full university status in 1873.

Located in Geneva, home to the United Nations' European headquarters and numerous international organizations, the university carries a strong academic reputation in international relations, law, and physics through its close collaboration with CERN.

items.name: University of Tartu
items.description: Founded by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden, Estonia's largest and oldest university.
history: Founded in 1632 by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden, the University of Tartu closed and reopened several times throughout its history due to wars and occupations, being permanently re-established in 1802.

Regarded as Estonia's national university, Tartu is today the country's largest and oldest university, and one of the Baltic region's leading research institutions in medicine, law, and natural sciences.

items.name: TalTech (Tallinn University of Technology)
items.description: Estonia's sole technical university, directly tied to the tech ecosystem of the capital, Tallinn.
history: Founded in 1918 as a private school called Tallinna Tehnikum (Tallinn College of Engineering), the institution was nationalized in 1920 and grew over time into Estonia's leading technical higher education institution.

Estonia's sole technical university, TalTech is closely tied to the country's strong digital economy and tech startups (the ecosystem that also produced Skype), and is the country's leading institution in computer science and engineering.

items.name: Lund University
items.description: Founded on territory Sweden had just conquered, one of the country's most international universities.
history: Founded by a charter from King Karl XI in 1666 in the Skåne region, which passed from Denmark to Sweden under the 1658 Treaty of Roskilde, with the aim of tying the region to Sweden, Lund University formally opened in 1668.

Today one of Sweden's largest and most international universities, Lund carries a strong research reputation in medicine, engineering, and physics, and is home to the renowned MAX IV and ESS research facilities.

items.name: Uppsala University
items.description: Founded in 1477, the oldest university in Scandinavia.
history: Founded with permission granted by Pope Sixtus IV on February 27, 1477, Uppsala University is the oldest university in Sweden and all of Scandinavia.
Having educated scientists such as botanist Carl Linnaeus and physicist Anders Celsius, Uppsala today maintains a strong academic tradition in medicine, natural sciences, and theology.
highlights: Scandinavia's oldest university, founded in 1477
Educated scientists like Carl Linnaeus and Anders Celsius
A strong academic tradition in medicine, natural sciences, and theology
pros: One of Scandinavia's most established and prestigious universities
A strong research tradition in medicine and natural sciences
A historic, student-friendly university town near Stockholm
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
Winters are long and dark
Some bachelor's programs are taught in Swedish

items.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
items.description: Sweden's largest and oldest technical university, at the heart of Scandinavia's engineering scene.
history: With roots reaching back to the Laboratorium Mechanicum, founded in 1697, KTH was established in 1827 as the Teknologiska Institutet (Institute of Technology), taking its current name, Kungliga Tekniska Högskolan (Royal Institute of Technology), in 1877.

Sweden's largest technical university, KTH is the country's leading institution in engineering, computer science, and architecture, directly tied to Stockholm's strong tech and startup ecosystem — the environment that also produced Spotify.
highlights: Sweden's largest and oldest technical university
A long scientific tradition with roots reaching back to 1697
Directly tied to Stockholm's strong tech and startup ecosystem
pros: Sweden's leading institution in engineering, computer science, and architecture
Direct proximity to Stockholm's strong tech sector, with internship access
A wide range of English-taught master's programs
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
Winters are long and dark
The program offering is largely limited to engineering and technical fields

items.name: Stockholm University
items.description: Founded as a radical alternative to the academic establishment, Sweden's fourth state university.
history: Founded in 1878 as Stockholm University College, conceived as a radical alternative to the traditional academic establishment of the time, the institution gained university status in 1960, becoming Sweden's fourth state university.
With a strong faculty in law, social sciences, and natural sciences, Stockholm University teaches in the Swedish capital, the same city that hosts the Nobel Prize ceremonies.
highlights: Founded as a radical alternative to the traditional academic establishment
Sweden's fourth state university
A strong faculty in law, social sciences, and natural sciences
pros: Direct proximity to career and cultural opportunities in Stockholm, Sweden's capital
A strong academic reputation in law and social sciences
A wide range of English-taught master's programs
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living, with student housing especially scarce in Stockholm
Winters are long and dark
Some bachelor's programs are taught in Swedish

items.name: KU Leuven
items.description: Founded in 1425, the oldest university in the Low Countries and the world's oldest Catholic university.
history: Founded by a papal bull issued by Pope Martin V on December 9, 1425, the University of Leuven is the oldest university in the Low Countries (today's Belgium/Netherlands region) and the oldest Catholic university still in operation in the world.

Consistently ranked among Europe's most innovative universities, KU Leuven today has a strong research reputation and a wide network of industry collaborations in engineering, medicine, and biotechnology.
highlights: The oldest university in the Low Countries, founded in 1425
The world's oldest Catholic university still in operation
Consistently ranked among Europe's most innovative universities
pros: A strong research reputation and industry collaboration in engineering, medicine, and biotechnology
Consistent ranking success as one of Europe's most innovative universities
Leuven is a safe, historic university town with a large student population
cons: Some bachelor's programs are taught in Dutch (Flemish)
Leuven is a small city compared to major urban centers
Competitive admission for popular subjects

items.name: Ghent University
items.description: Founded by King William I of the Netherlands, one of Belgium's largest research universities.
history: Founded in 1817 by King William I of the Netherlands, Ghent University has changed its language of instruction several times since its founding; today it is a fully Dutch (Flemish)-taught institution.

Known for its iconic Boekentoren (Book Tower) library building, a landmark of the city, Ghent University is today one of Belgium's strongest research universities in biotechnology, veterinary science, and engineering.
highlights: Founded by King William I of the Netherlands in 1817
Known for its iconic Boekentoren (Book Tower) library building
A strong research reputation in biotechnology, veterinary science, and engineering
pros: A strong research reputation in biotechnology and veterinary sciences
Ghent is a lively, student-friendly city famous for its medieval architecture
A more affordable cost of living compared to Brussels
cons: The large majority of bachelor's programs are taught in Dutch
English program options are largely limited to the master's level
Belgium's variable, rainy climate

items.name: Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB)
items.description: Founded on the principle of "free inquiry," Brussels' major French-speaking university.
history: Founded in 1834 by lawyer and liberal politician Pierre-Théodore Verhaegen on the principle of "free inquiry" (libre examen), as a reaction to the Catholic Church's dominance over education at the time, the university took its current French-speaking structure in 1970 when the Dutch-speaking VUB split off.
Teaching in the heart of Brussels, close to the European Union institutions, ULB carries a strong academic reputation in social sciences, law, and medicine.
highlights: Founded in 1834 on the principle of "free inquiry" (libre examen)
Took its current structure in 1970 when the Dutch-speaking VUB split off
Located close to the European Union institutions
pros: Direct proximity to the European Union institutions, with internship and career opportunities
A strong academic reputation in social sciences, law, and medicine
Brussels' multicultural, international environment
cons: Most bachelor's programs are taught in French
Brussels is one of Belgium's more expensive cities
Competitive admission for popular subjects

items.name: Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB)
items.description: Brussels' Dutch-speaking university, born from the linguistic split of a university founded in 1834.
history: With roots reaching back to the Université libre de Bruxelles, founded by Pierre-Théodore Verhaegen in 1834, VUB became an independent institution in 1970 when that university split along linguistic lines.
Teaching on a modern campus in Brussels' Etterbeek district, VUB has a strong faculty in social sciences, engineering, and medicine, and maintains close collaboration with ULB across many programs.
highlights: An independent university born from ULB's 1970 linguistic split
A modern campus in Brussels' Etterbeek district
Close collaboration with ULB across many programs
pros: Direct proximity to Brussels' international, multicultural environment
A broad academic network through joint programs with ULB
A solid faculty in social sciences and engineering
cons: Most bachelor's programs are taught in Dutch
Brussels is one of Belgium's more expensive cities
Less international name recognition than KU Leuven

items.name: University of Copenhagen
items.description: Founded in 1479, one of the oldest universities in Denmark and Northern Europe.
history: Opening on June 1, 1479, after King Christian I received permission from Pope Sixtus IV, the University of Copenhagen was founded on the German university model with faculties of theology, law, medicine, and philosophy.

Having educated figures including physicist Niels Bohr, the University of Copenhagen is today Denmark's largest university and one of Scandinavia's leading research institutions in medicine, law, and natural sciences.
highlights: Denmark's oldest university, founded in 1479
A scientific legacy that includes physicist Niels Bohr
Denmark's largest university and one of Scandinavia's leading research institutions
pros: A strong, established academic reputation in medicine, law, and natural sciences
Copenhagen's high quality of life and bike-friendly city culture
A wide range of English-taught master's programs
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
Student housing can be difficult to find in Copenhagen
Some bachelor's programs are taught in Danish

items.name: DTU (Technical University of Denmark)
items.description: Founded at the initiative of physicist Hans Christian Ørsted, Denmark's leading engineering university.
history: Founded in 1829 at the initiative of physicist Hans Christian Ørsted, the discoverer of electromagnetism, as Denmark's first polytechnic school, DTU grew over time into the country's leading engineering university.
Today teaching at its campus in Kongens Lyngby north of Copenhagen, DTU ranks among Europe's leading technical universities in biotechnology, sustainable energy, and engineering.
highlights: Denmark's first polytechnic school, founded in 1829 at the initiative of Hans Christian Ørsted
Denmark's leading engineering university
Europe-wide recognition in sustainable energy and biotechnology
pros: One of Europe's leading research institutions in sustainable energy and biotechnology
Direct proximity to Denmark's strong wind energy and green tech sector
A wide range of English-taught master's programs
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
The program offering is almost entirely limited to engineering and technical fields
Kongens Lyngby is somewhat removed from central Copenhagen

items.name: Aarhus University
items.description: Denmark's second-largest and youngest established university, known for its yellow-brick architecture.
history: Founded in 1928, Aarhus University became Denmark's first university outside Copenhagen, launched through donations from the local business community and public.

Known for its iconic yellow-brick buildings and a campus set among parkland, Aarhus is today Denmark's second-largest university, with a strong academic reputation in business, medicine, and agricultural sciences.
highlights: Denmark's first university outside Copenhagen (1928)
Iconic yellow-brick architecture on a park-like campus
A strong academic reputation in business, medicine, and agricultural sciences
pros: A strong, modern academic reputation in business and medicine
A green, student-friendly campus set among parkland
A more affordable cost of living compared to Copenhagen
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
Less international name recognition than Copenhagen
Some bachelor's programs are taught in Danish

items.name: Copenhagen Business School (CBS)
items.description: One of Northern Europe's largest business schools.
history: Founded in 1917 by the Danish Society for the Advancement of Business Education, CBS was integrated into Denmark's official higher education system in 1965.
Known for its iconic "Kilen" (The Wedge) building, CBS is today one of Northern Europe's largest business schools, with a strong academic reputation in business, economics, and international trade.
highlights: Founded in 1917, one of Northern Europe's largest business schools
Known for its iconic "Kilen" (The Wedge) building
A strong academic reputation in business, economics, and international trade
pros: One of Northern Europe's strongest schools in business and international trade
Copenhagen's high quality of life and international business environment
A wide range of English-taught master's and MBA programs
cons: Scandinavia's high cost of living
The program is entirely limited to business and economics
Student housing can be difficult to find in Copenhagen

hero.title: About Studiva
hero.subtitle: Founded in 2026 for students who want to study in Europe, we're a consultancy focused on studying abroad.

story.title: Our Story
paragraphs: Studiva was founded in Istanbul in 2026 with the goal of helping students reach Europe's leading universities through a transparent, trustworthy process.

We're a team with up-to-date knowledge of 60+ universities across Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, France, Switzerland, Scandinavia, and Belgium, closely following each country's application system, visa requirements, and academic calendar.

Every student's academic background, budget, and goals are different — that's why we help you choose the right country and university instead of forcing you into one template. As a newly founded company, we offer a concrete commitment instead of inflated numbers: an admission guarantee when you complete our process in full.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: To ensure every student reaches the European university best suited to their academic potential and dreams through a transparent, trustworthy process backed by an admission guarantee.
